definition: A judgment that an accused person is not guilty of the charge. After an acquittal, the person may not be retried for the same offence (double jeopardy).
plainLanguageSummary: When the court decides the accused is not guilty. The case ends there, and the state cannot bring the same charge again.

definition: Latin for 'guilty act'. The physical element of a crime, the prohibited act or omission itself. A crime generally requires both actus reus and mens rea together.
plainLanguageSummary: The 'guilty act', the actual doing of the wrong thing. For most crimes, both the bad action and a guilty intention must be present together.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act

definition: The postponement of a court hearing or trial to a later date, often granted for reasons such as preparation time, absence of a party or witness, or the court's convenience.
plainLanguageSummary: The court moves a hearing to another day. It happens for many reasons, like needing more time to prepare or a witness not showing up.

definition: The quality of evidence that allows it to be considered by a court. Evidence may be excluded if irrelevant, unfairly prejudicial, hearsay or obtained through improper means.
plainLanguageSummary: Whether a court will let evidence in. Even real evidence can be rejected if it was obtained illegally or is hearsay. Inadmissible evidence cannot be used.

definition: A court order that legally transfers parental rights and responsibilities for a child from biological parents to adoptive parents, making the child a legal member of the new family.
plainLanguageSummary: Legally becoming the parent of a child who is not yours by birth. Once adopted, the child has all the rights of a biological child.
citations: Child Rights Act 2003; Adoption Laws of various states

definition: A doctrine by which a person who openly occupies another's land continuously and without permission for a statutory period may acquire title to it, extinguishing the owner's right.
plainLanguageSummary: If someone occupies land openly and unchallenged for many years, they can eventually become the legal owner. Owners who abandon land can lose it this way.
citations: Limitation Laws of various Nigerian states

definition: A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, for use as evidence in court. It is one of the most common legal documents used in Nigerian courts.
plainLanguageSummary: A written statement where you swear that everything in it is true, just like if you were speaking in court. It's used as evidence and lying in one is a serious offence , it's the same as perjury.

definition: A legal relationship where one person (the agent) is authorised to act on behalf of another (the principal) to create legal relations with third parties.
plainLanguageSummary: When you appoint someone to act for you , like hiring a lawyer to represent you or giving a real estate agent authority to sell your property. The agent's actions legally bind you.

definition: A defence claim that the accused was elsewhere when the offence was committed, and therefore could not have committed it. An alibi must generally be raised and proven by the accused.
plainLanguageSummary: 'I was somewhere else when it happened.' If you have evidence you were far away at the time of the crime, you can use that as a defence.

definition: A range of methods for resolving disputes outside of the traditional courtroom process, including arbitration, mediation, conciliation, and negotiation.
plainLanguageSummary: Ways to settle disagreements without going to court. Arbitration, mediation, negotiation , all of these are faster, cheaper, and more private than a full-blown lawsuit.
citations: Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023; various court ADR rules

definition: Latin for 'friend of the court'. A person or organisation, not a party to a case, who volunteers information or arguments to assist the court in deciding a matter of general public importance.
plainLanguageSummary: A 'friend of the court' who is not part of the case but helps the judges by providing expert input, often in big public-interest matters. Their role is to assist, not to take sides in the usual sense.
citations: Court of Appeal Rules; Supreme Court Rules

definition: The statutory yearly meeting of a company's shareholders where accounts, dividends, directors and appointment of auditors are considered. Failure to hold AGMs is an offence.
plainLanguageSummary: The company's yearly shareholders gathering. Financial results are presented, directors may be chosen and big decisions are voted on.
citations: Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, Sections 229-230

definition: A request to a higher court to review and change the decision of a lower court. Appeals are based on errors of law, procedure or, in limited cases, findings of fact.
plainLanguageSummary: When you believe the court got it wrong, you ask a higher court to re-examine the decision. You are not starting over, you are asking for a review of the errors.

definition: The power of a higher court to review decisions and change outcomes of decisions of lower courts. Most appellate jurisdiction is legislatively created.
plainLanguageSummary: If you lose in a lower court, you can appeal to a higher court. That higher court doesn't redo the whole trial , they check if the lower court made legal mistakes. That power to review is called appellate jurisdiction.

definition: A form of alternative dispute resolution where parties agree to submit their dispute to one or more arbitrators whose decision is binding, instead of going to court.
plainLanguageSummary: Instead of going to court, you and the other person agree to let a neutral third party (the arbitrator) decide who's right. It's faster and more private than a lawsuit, and the decision is final.

definition: The procedure by which an accused person is brought before a court to hear the charges against them and to enter a plea (guilty, not guilty, or no contest).
plainLanguageSummary: The first time you stand in court after being charged. The judge reads out what you're accused of, and you say whether you plead guilty or not guilty. It's the formal start of the trial process.

definition: The act of apprehending a person suspected of committing an offence, typically by law enforcement officers, in accordance with legal procedures.
plainLanguageSummary: When the police pick you up because they think you've broken the law. There are rules about how it has to happen , they usually need a warrant, and they have to tell you why you're being arrested.

definition: The internal rulebook of a company regulating how it is governed, including the conduct of meetings, appointment of directors, shares and distribution of profits.
plainLanguageSummary: The company's internal rulebook: how meetings run, how directors are chosen and how profits are shared. It binds the company and its members.

definition: Two related torts: assault is creating a reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful contact, while battery is the actual unlawful physical contact. Both are actionable in civil law and may be crimes.
plainLanguageSummary: Assault is making someone fear they are about to be hit; battery is the actual hitting. Both can give you a civil claim and be criminal offences.
citations: Common law principles; Criminal Code Act

definition: The transfer of rights, property or the benefit and burden of a contract from one person to another. The transferor is the assignor and the receiver the assignee.
plainLanguageSummary: Passing your rights in a contract or property to someone else. For example, a landlord assigning a lease or a creditor assigning a debt.

definition: Protection granted by a state to a person fleeing persecution in their home country on grounds of race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a group.
plainLanguageSummary: Protection given to someone forced to leave their country because they are being persecuted. They can stay and are not sent back to danger.
citations: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights; UN Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees

definition: The temporary release of an accused person awaiting trial, usually on payment of a sum of money or other security as guarantee of their appearance in court.
plainLanguageSummary: If you're charged with a crime but haven't been convicted yet, you might be allowed to go home while waiting for your trial , as long as you promise to come back to court. Sometimes you need to pay money or provide a guarantor.
citations: Section 35(4), 1999 Constitution of Nigeria; Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015

definition: The principle that to prove the content of a document, the original document should be produced unless its absence is adequately explained and a valid exception applies.
plainLanguageSummary: When a document matters, the court wants the original, not a photocopy or someone's memory of it. Copies are allowed only if the original is genuinely unavailable.

definition: A document issued by a carrier acknowledging receipt of goods for shipment, serving as a receipt, a contract of carriage and evidence of title to the goods.
plainLanguageSummary: The shipping receipt that proves goods were loaded on a vessel and represents who owns them. Whoever holds it can claim the goods at the destination.
citations: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, Cap C2, LFN 2004

definition: The failure of one party to fulfil their obligations under a contract without a lawful excuse. The innocent party may claim damages or seek specific performance.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone breaks their side of the deal. Maybe they didn't deliver the goods, didn't do the work, or didn't pay. The other party can sue for compensation or ask the court to force performance.

definition: The offer, giving, solicitation or acceptance of an undue advantage in exchange for improper performance of a duty, often by a public official.
plainLanguageSummary: Giving or taking money or favours to get someone in power to do something improperly. Gifting money to a public official for favourable treatment is bribery.
citations: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000

definition: The obligation to prove the facts of a case. In criminal cases the prosecution bears the burden of proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt; in civil cases the claimant proves on the balance of probabilities.
plainLanguageSummary: Whoever makes an accusation must prove it. In criminal cases, the state must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt. In civil cases, you only need to show your side is more likely true.

definition: A registered trading name under which an individual or partnership carries on business, registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission. It does not give a separate legal personality.
plainLanguageSummary: A name you register for your business that is not a full company. Unlike a company, it has no separate legal identity, so you remain personally liable.

definition: The legal ability to enter a binding contract. Persons below the age of majority, those of unsound mind and some other classes lack full capacity to contract.
plainLanguageSummary: Who the law allows to make a binding deal. Minors and people without full mental capacity generally cannot be bound the same way adults can.

definition: The fact or set of facts that give a person the right to seek judicial relief against another party. It is the legal basis for a lawsuit.
plainLanguageSummary: The reason you're suing. Something happened , a broken contract, an injury, a property dispute , and that event gives you the legal right to go to court. That event is your cause of action.
citations: Civil Procedure rules; various Nigerian statutes

definition: A formal notice lodged in the land registry or court warning that a particular land transaction must not be completed without the caveator being notified or heard.
plainLanguageSummary: A red flag placed on a property's records so it cannot be quietly sold or transferred without you being alerted. Common in land disputes and probate matters.

definition: A Latin phrase meaning 'let the buyer beware.' It places the responsibility on the buyer to examine and assess the quality and suitability of goods before purchasing.
plainLanguageSummary: Before you buy something, it's your job to check it out. If you buy a phone without testing it and it turns out to be faulty, the law says you should have checked first. (Though consumer protection laws have softened this rule.)
citations: Common law principle; Sale of Goods Act, Cap S1, LFN 2004

definition: The document issued by a Governor evidencing a statutory right of occupancy over land, regularly required for land transactions, mortgages and compensation purposes.
plainLanguageSummary: The government-issued paper proving you hold a piece of land under the Land Use Act. Banks want it before lending on land, and it protects your ownership.
citations: Land Use Act, Cap L5, LFN 2004

definition: A security interest over an asset (such as land, shares or goods) that gives the holder the ability to enforce repayment of a debt from the asset upon default.
plainLanguageSummary: A legal claim someone holds over your asset as security for a debt. If you default, they can take the asset to recover what you owe.

definition: The system that allows each branch of government to amend or veto acts of another branch so as to prevent any one branch from exerting too much power.
plainLanguageSummary: Each part of government can keep the others in check. The President can veto a law, the National Assembly can override the veto, and the courts can declare the law unconstitutional. Nobody gets unchecked power.

definition: A written order by a person to their bank to pay a stated sum to a named person or bearer from their account. Dishonoured cheques create legal liability.
plainLanguageSummary: A written instruction telling your bank to pay someone a certain amount from your account. If the bank refuses payment, the cheque is 'dishonoured' and can lead to claims.
citations: Bills of Exchange Act, Cap B8, LFN 2004

definition: The special rights and protections granted to persons under 18, including the right to survival, education, protection from abuse, exploitation and harmful labour under the Child Rights Act.
plainLanguageSummary: Children under 18 have extra protection. They must be cared for, educated and guarded from abuse, early marriage and harmful work. These are special rights just for them.

definition: Evidence from which a fact may be inferred, rather than evidence that proves it directly. A chain of circumstances can support a verdict if consistent and convincing.
plainLanguageSummary: Based on surrounding facts rather than someone seeing it directly. Like fingerprints and a motive pointing to the culprit. Many facts can add up to strong proof.

definition: The legal status of belonging to a state, with its rights and duties. In Nigeria, citizenship may be by birth, registration or naturalisation.
plainLanguageSummary: Being a legal member of a country. Nigerians get citizenship by birth, by marriage or registration, or by naturalisation after years of residence.

definition: A lawsuit brought by one or more representatives on behalf of a large group of people with similar claims, so they can pursue relief together.
plainLanguageSummary: When a group of people harmed the same way sue together through representatives, like thousands of customers defrauded by one company.

definition: The negotiation between employers (or their associations) and trade unions over wages, working conditions and other terms of employment.
plainLanguageSummary: Unions and employers sitting down to negotiate pay and conditions for all workers together, rather than each person negotiating alone.
citations: Trade Unions Act, Cap T14, LFN 2004

definition: A legal person created by incorporation under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, with an identity separate from its owners, limited liability and perpetual succession.
plainLanguageSummary: A business entity that is its own legal person. It can own property, sue and be sued, and owners' risk is limited to what they invested.

definition: A dispute resolution process where a neutral third party meets separately with the parties to narrow differences and encourage a settlement, unlike mediation where the parties meet together.
plainLanguageSummary: A neutral person talks to each side separately to help them settle, shuttling between them to narrow the gap. It is a softer, private way to resolve disputes.

definition: Something of value exchanged between parties to a contract. Each party must give something (a promise, act, or forbearance) for the contract to be legally enforceable.
plainLanguageSummary: The 'price' of the deal. Both sides have to give something up , money, services, a promise. If only one side gives something, it's a gift, not a contract, and the law won't enforce it.

definition: The supreme body of laws, rules and principles that establishes the structure of a state, defines the powers of government and guarantees the rights of citizens. In Nigeria, the 1999 Constitution is the ground norm that all other laws are measured against.
plainLanguageSummary: The highest law of the land. Every other law, government action and court decision must agree with the Constitution. If a law contradicts it, the courts can declare that law invalid.
citations: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended)

definition: Laws and regulations designed to ensure that products and services sold to consumers meet acceptable standards of safety, quality, and fairness.
plainLanguageSummary: The law has your back when you shop. If you buy something dangerous, defective, or misrepresented, consumer protection laws let you get a refund, replacement, or compensation.
citations: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018

definition: Conduct that disobeys, disrespects or interferes with the authority of a court, such as disobeying an order or publishing material that prejudices a trial. It may be punished by fine or imprisonment.
plainLanguageSummary: Disrespecting the court or ignoring its orders, like refusing to obey an injunction or publishing prejudicial comments during a trial. It can result in fine or jail time.
citations: Sheriffs and Civil Process Act, Cap S6, LFN 2004

definition: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties that creates mutual obligations enforceable by law. A valid contract requires offer, acceptance, consideration, and intention to create legal relations.
plainLanguageSummary: A deal that the law will enforce. If you agree to do something for someone and they agree to pay you, that's a contract. If one side breaks the deal, the other can go to court about it.
citations: Contract Act, Cap C21, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004

definition: A defence where the claimant's own carelessness contributed to their injury, reducing the damages they can recover in proportion to their share of fault.
plainLanguageSummary: If you were partly at fault for your own injury (like not wearing a helmet), the damages you recover can be reduced by your share of the blame.

definition: A judgment by a court that an accused person is guilty of a crime, usually followed by sentencing. It requires proof of guilt to the criminal standard.
plainLanguageSummary: When the court finds someone guilty after a fair trial. It is followed by sentencing, which is the punishment phase.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015

definition: A type of intellectual property that grants the creator of an original work exclusive rights to its use and distribution, typically for a limited time.
plainLanguageSummary: Once you create something original , a book, song, video, software , the law automatically gives you the right to decide who can use, copy, or sell it. No one can use your work without your permission.

definition: The unauthorised use, reproduction, distribution or performance of a copyrighted work, violating the owner's exclusive rights. Remedies include injunctions, damages and accounts of profits.
plainLanguageSummary: Using someone's book, song, film or software without permission. The owner can sue for compensation and get the court to stop the use.

definition: The abuse of public office or entrusted power for private gain, including bribery, embezzlement, extortion and nepotism. It is criminalised under dedicated anti-corruption statutes.
plainLanguageSummary: When people in power misuse their office for personal gain, like stealing public funds or collecting bribes. It is punishable under anti-corruption laws.
citations: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000; EFCC Act 2004

definition: The expenses of litigation that a court may order the losing party to pay to the successful party, including filing fees, counsel fees and service charges.
plainLanguageSummary: After a case, the judge can order the losing side to pay part of the winner's legal expenses. This stops people from dragging others to court over nothing.

definition: The second highest court in Nigeria which hears appeals from the High Courts, Federal High Court and other lower tribunals. It sits in divisions across the country.
plainLanguageSummary: The middle appeal court. If you lose in a High Court, you appeal here first. Several divisions sit in different parts of Nigeria to bring justice closer.

definition: The principal statute defining criminal offences and their punishment in the southern states of Nigeria, covering offences against persons, property and public order.
plainLanguageSummary: The big law book that lists crimes and their punishments used in most southern states. If an act is not listed as a crime here, it is not an offence.
citations: Criminal Code Act, Cap C38, LFN 2004

definition: The legal representation and arguments advanced on behalf of an accused person, ensuring the presumption of innocence, fair hearing and legal safeguards are respected.
plainLanguageSummary: The accused person's side of the story, presented by their lawyer. It tests the prosecution's case and enforces the rule that you are innocent until proven guilty.

definition: Conduct that falls so far below the standard of care expected of a reasonable person that it becomes a crime, usually where it causes death or serious injury.
plainLanguageSummary: Carelessness so extreme that it becomes a crime, especially when it costs lives, like a reckless driver killing someone. It is worse than ordinary carelessness.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act

definition: The questioning of a witness by the opposing party after examination-in-chief, to test the truthfulness and accuracy of their evidence. Leading questions are allowed.
plainLanguageSummary: The other side's lawyer gets to question your witness to test whether what they said is true. This is where contradictions and weaknesses in a story come out.

definition: The legal right and responsibility to care for and make decisions for a child. Courts decide custody based on the welfare and best interests of the child.
plainLanguageSummary: Who the children live with and who makes decisions for them after a split. Courts focus on what is best for the child, not which parent 'deserves' them.
citations: Child Rights Act 2003; Matrimonial Causes Act

definition: A court that applies customary law in civil matters such as marriage, inheritance and land disputes, following the customs of the community it serves.
plainLanguageSummary: A local court that applies community customs rather than written statutes. It is used for things like customary marriage, small land disputes and family matters.

definition: Land ownership and use governed by the customs of a community, where land is often held by families or communities through traditional heads, subject to customary rules.
plainLanguageSummary: Land rules passed down by community tradition, where families or communities hold land through their chiefs or heads. Custom controls how it is used and passed on.
citations: Land Use Act, Cap L5, LFN 2004

definition: A marriage contracted according to the customs of a community, which may involve bride price and traditional rites. It is valid, though not registered under the Marriage Act.
plainLanguageSummary: A marriage done the traditional way, with bride price and family ceremonies. It is legally valid, even though it is not registered at a government registry.

definition: Criminal activity carried out using computers or the internet, such as phishing, identity theft, hacking, online fraud and child exploitation online.
plainLanguageSummary: Crimes committed with computers or phones: hacking accounts, phishing for passwords, ATM fraud or online scams. Nigeria has specific laws against these.

definition: A sum of money claimed by, or awarded to, a person as compensation for loss or injury caused by the wrongful act of another party.
plainLanguageSummary: Money the court orders someone to pay you because they hurt you or broke a deal. It's not punishment , it's meant to put you back in the position you'd have been in if they hadn't messed up.

definition: The legal framework, principally the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, governing the collection, processing and transfer of personal data, requiring consent, transparency and security.
plainLanguageSummary: Rules about how companies handle your personal information. They must ask permission, tell you how it is used and protect it from leaks. You have rights over your data.

definition: A formal written legal document, usually under seal, used to transfer title to property or evidence rights and obligations. Examples include conveyances and assents.
plainLanguageSummary: A formal signed and sealed document that transfers property or creates legal rights. Properly executed deeds are the backbone of property deals.

definition: The act of communicating false statements that injure the reputation of a person or entity. In Nigeria, both libel (written) and slander (spoken) are recognized forms of defamation.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone tells lies about you that damage your reputation. If it's written or posted online, it's libel. If it's spoken, it's slander. You can sue for compensation.

definition: A judgment entered against a defendant who fails to file a defence or appears in court within the required time, without the case going to full trial.
plainLanguageSummary: If you are sued and you ignore it or fail to file your defence on time, the court can award judgment against you automatically, without hearing your side.

definition: Rules, regulations and by-laws made by bodies other than the legislature, when the legislature has delegated lawmaking power to them. Examples include ministerial regulations and local government by-laws.
plainLanguageSummary: Laws made by government agencies and officials, not by parliament. Parliament gives them the power through a parent law. If the agency goes beyond that power, the law is invalid.

definition: The expulsion of a foreign national from a country, ordered by the government when their presence is illegal or contrary to the public interest.
plainLanguageSummary: Being officially sent out of a country because your stay is illegal or unwelcome. Those facing deportation have rights to legal process.

definition: The exemption of accredited diplomats and their families from the criminal and civil jurisdiction of the host state, based on international conventions and reciprocity.
plainLanguageSummary: Diplomats cannot normally be arrested or sued in the country where they are posted. It protects international relations but has limits.

definition: Evidence that directly proves a fact in issue without requiring inference, such as an eyewitness describing the event they saw. It may be tested by cross-examination.
plainLanguageSummary: Evidence that points straight at the fact, like a witness who actually saw the incident. It is the strongest and most straightforward kind of proof.

definition: The pre-trial process by which parties obtain evidence and information held by the other side, including documents and answers to written questions, before trial.
plainLanguageSummary: Before trial, each side gets to see the other's documents and relevant information. It stops surprises in court and helps both sides prepare fairly.

definition: The legal dissolution of a marriage by a court, ending the marital relationship and resolving property, custody and maintenance issues.
plainLanguageSummary: The legal end of a marriage. Courts grant divorce on grounds like breakdown of the relationship, then settle property, children and support.
citations: Matrimonial Causes Act, Cap M7, LFN 2004

definition: Evidence contained in documents that is presented to prove a fact, such as contracts, letters, ledgers and records. It often requires authentication and may be subject to the best evidence rule.
plainLanguageSummary: Proof in paper or digital form: agreements, messages, receipts, bank records. Documents can be powerful proof, but originals are preferred over copies.

definition: Abusive behaviour by one member of a household against another, including physical assault, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, stalking and economic control.
plainLanguageSummary: Abuse at home: a partner or family member hurting you physically, emotionally or financially. It is a crime and there are protection orders and legal remedies.

definition: A constitutional protection preventing a person from being tried again for an offence for which they have already been convicted or acquitted.
plainLanguageSummary: You cannot be tried twice for the same crime. If a court acquits or convicts you, the state cannot drag you back to court for the same offence.

definition: The legal requirement that the state must respect all legal rights owed to a person. It guarantees fair treatment through the judicial system according to established rules and principles.
plainLanguageSummary: The government has to follow the rules when dealing with you. They can't just skip steps or make up procedures , there's a proper way to do things, and they have to follow it.

definition: Pressure, threats or violence inflicted on a person to force them into a contract or act. A contract signed under duress is voidable.
plainLanguageSummary: Signing a deal because you were threatened or pressured. An agreement forced this way can be set aside by the victim.

definition: A legal obligation to adhere to a standard of reasonable care while performing any acts that could foreseeably harm others. It is the first element that must be proven in a negligence claim.
plainLanguageSummary: If you're doing something that could hurt someone, the law says you must be careful. A doctor owes a duty to patients, a driver owes a duty to other road users. Break that duty, and you're liable.

definition: A legal right of a landowner to use another person's land in a defined way, such as a right of way, right of drainage or right to support. It attaches to the land, not the owner.
plainLanguageSummary: The right to use part of someone else's land for a specific purpose, like a road through their property to reach yours. It travels with bundling the land.

definition: A legal challenge to the result of an election, filed by a candidate or voter who alleges that the election was not conducted fairly or in accordance with electoral laws.
plainLanguageSummary: If you believe an election was rigged or conducted unfairly, you can take the matter to court. Election petitions have strict timelines and rules , the courts must decide them quickly.

definition: Special courts established to hear and determine disputes arising from elections in Nigeria. They include the National and State Houses of Assembly Election Tribunals and the Governorship Election Tribunals.
plainLanguageSummary: When election results are disputed, they don't go to regular courts , they go to special election tribunals set up just for that purpose. They're faster than regular courts because election disputes need quick resolution.
citations: Third Schedule, 1999 Constitution of Nigeria; Electoral Act 2022

definition: Commercial and legal activities conducted electronically, validated by legislation that gives digital contracts, signatures and records the same effect as paper ones.
plainLanguageSummary: Doing deals digitally: signing contracts online, buying with cards and keeping electronic records. The law treats valid digital signatures like paper ones.

definition: An agreement between employer and employee setting out the terms of work, including duties, remuneration, hours, leave and termination conditions.
plainLanguageSummary: The deal that governs your job: what you do, what you are paid, hours and how either side can end it. You should get a written copy.

definition: The process of making an arbitration award binding and executable, by application to a court that is required to recognise and enforce the award subject to limited grounds.
plainLanguageSummary: If someone refuses to obey an arbitration ruling, you go to court to make it enforceable, almost like a court judgment. Grounds to refuse are very narrow.

definition: The legal process by which a person whose fundamental rights have been, or are likely to be, violated can seek redress in court through a Fundamental Rights Enforcement Procedure.
plainLanguageSummary: If someone violates your constitutional rights, you don't need to wait. You can go straight to court with a special application to protect and restore those rights quickly.

definition: A mandatory evaluation of the likely environmental effects of a proposed project before approval, required for major developments to prevent or mitigate environmental damage.
plainLanguageSummary: Checking a big project's effect on the environment before it is built. Large projects cannot proceed without this study and approval.
citations: Environmental Impact Assessment Act, Cap E12, LFN 2004

definition: The constitutional guarantee that every citizen shall have equal rights and opportunities, and shall not be discriminated against on grounds of ethnicity, sex, religion or political opinion.
plainLanguageSummary: The law treats every citizen the same. You cannot be denied opportunities or access because of your tribe, sex, religion or political views.

definition: The process of managing and distributing a deceased person's estate, including collecting assets, paying debts, and distributing remaining property to beneficiaries.
plainLanguageSummary: After someone dies, someone has to take charge , gather their assets, pay their debts, and give what's left to the right people. That whole process is estate administration.

definition: A principle preventing a person from asserting a fact or right that contradicts what they previously said or did, when the other party relied on the earlier position.
plainLanguageSummary: You cannot say one thing, then turn around and say the opposite if someone relied on your first position. Consistency is enforced by this rule.

definition: Anything that tends to prove or disprove a fact in issue in a case, including testimony, documents, objects and electronic records. It is regulated by the Evidence Act.
plainLanguageSummary: The proof used to convince a court, like witness stories, papers, photos or video. Rules decide what counts and how strong it must be.

definition: The stage of a trial where a party questions its own witness to present evidence in support of its case. Leading questions are generally not permitted at this stage.
plainLanguageSummary: When your lawyer asks your own witness to tell the court what happened. The witness gives their account freely, without the lawyer feeding them answers.

definition: A rule or directive issued by the President or a Governor in the exercise of executive powers, which has the force of law but must not contradict the Constitution or statutes.
plainLanguageSummary: When the President or a Governor makes a rule using their executive power without waiting for parliament. It operates like law, but it can be challenged in court if it oversteps.

definition: A witness with specialised knowledge, skill or training whose opinion evidence assists the court on technical matters beyond the ordinary knowledge of the judge.
plainLanguageSummary: A specialist, like a doctor or engineer, whose professional opinion helps the court understand technical issues. They testify about what experts conclude, not only facts.

definition: The formal process by which one state surrenders a person accused or convicted of a crime to another state where they face prosecution or imprisonment.
plainLanguageSummary: Handing a suspect over to another country to face justice there. It happens under treaties and follows strict rules.

definition: A statutory exception allowing limited use of copyrighted works without permission for purposes such as research, private study, criticism or news reporting.
plainLanguageSummary: You can sometimes use short parts of protected works without asking, like quoting a book for a review or research, as long as the use is fair.

definition: The unlawful restraint of a person's freedom of movement without lawful justification, such as being detained by a shopkeeper or private person without grounds.
plainLanguageSummary: Being locked up or held against your will without legal authority. A shop that detains you without evidence can be sued, even if you were released later.

definition: A court of first instance with jurisdiction over federal matters such as revenue and taxation, customs, banking, companies, intellectual property and federal offences.
plainLanguageSummary: The court that handles federal issues: tax disputes, customs, companies, trademarks, patents and federal criminal cases. It sits in states, but it decides federal matters.

definition: A serious crime, generally punishable by imprisonment, often for several years or life. Examples include murder, armed robbery and treason.
plainLanguageSummary: A major crime like murder, robbery or treason. Convictions bring heavy punishment, usually lengthy jail time.

definition: A legal obligation to act in the best interest of another party. A fiduciary must not profit from their position and must avoid conflicts of interest.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone trusts you to handle their affairs, the law says you MUST put their interests first , not yours. If you're a lawyer, trustee, or financial advisor, you can't use their money or information for your own gain.
citations: Common law principles; Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020

definition: A contract clause that frees both parties from liability when performance is prevented by extraordinary events beyond their control, such as natural disasters, war or epidemics.
plainLanguageSummary: The 'act of God' clause. If an extraordinary event like a flood or war makes the deal impossible, neither side is treated as having breached.
citations: Common law principles; contract drafting practice

definition: The right to vote in public elections; also known as suffrage. In Nigeria, every citizen who is 18 or older and registered has the franchise.
plainLanguageSummary: Your right to vote. Once you're 18 and registered, you have the franchise , the power to choose who represents you in government. It's one of the most fundamental rights in a democracy.
citations: Section 77, 1999 Constitution of Nigeria; Electoral Act 2022

definition: A dishonest deception intended to make a person part with money, property or rights, or act to their detriment. It is both a crime and a civil wrong.
plainLanguageSummary: Tricking someone out of their money or property using lies and deception. An advance-fee ('419') scam is a classic example.
citations: Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act 2006

definition: The fundamental right not to be subjected to torture, inhuman or degrading treatment, or slavery and forced labour. The Constitution expressly prohibits these practices.
plainLanguageSummary: Nobody, including the police, can torture you, abuse you or treat you in a degrading way. Involuntary servitude and forced labour are also banned.

definition: The fundamental right to assemble peacefully and associate freely with others, including forming or joining political parties, unions and other groups.
plainLanguageSummary: You can gather with others peacefully and form or join groups, from unions to political parties. The only limit is that the gathering must be peaceful and lawful.

definition: The fundamental right to hold opinions and receive or impart ideas and information without interference. It protects speech, writing, artistic work and online expression, subject to lawful limits.
plainLanguageSummary: You can say what you think, write, post and create without the government stopping you. Limits exist for law and order, national security and protecting other people's reputation.

definition: The fundamental right to practice, observe and propagate one's religion, or to change one's religion, freely. This right includes the use of religious buildings in accordance with custom.
plainLanguageSummary: You can worship however you choose, change your religion, or follow none at all, and the state cannot punish you for it. Everyone's faith practices are protected equally.

definition: The automatic discharge of a contract when an unforeseen event, through no fault of either party, makes performance impossible, illegal or radically different from what was agreed.
plainLanguageSummary: When something unexpected and unavoidable (a flood, a ban) makes a contract impossible to perform. Both sides are freed without blame.

definition: Rights guaranteed to every citizen by the Constitution, including the right to life, personal liberty, freedom of expression, freedom of religion, and the right to peaceful assembly.
plainLanguageSummary: The basic rights the Constitution gives you just for being a Nigerian citizen , like the right to speak freely, move freely, and not be treated unfairly by the government.

definition: A promise by one person (the guarantor) to be responsible for the debt or obligation of another if that person defaults. It is a secondary obligation dependent on the principal debtor.
plainLanguageSummary: Standing surety for someone else's debt. If they fail to pay, the creditor can come after you because you guaranteed the repayment.

definition: A legal writ requiring a person who has detained another to bring the detainee before a court and justify the detention. It is a fundamental safeguard against unlawful imprisonment.
plainLanguageSummary: If someone is locked up without a good reason, a judge can order their release. It's basically the law saying 'you can't just hold people without explaining why.'

definition: A statement made by a person other than the witness testifying, offered to prove the truth of the matter stated. It is generally inadmissible subject to statutory exceptions.
plainLanguageSummary: Second-hand evidence: 'I heard that he said'. Courts usually reject it because the original speaker cannot be questioned. There are limited exceptions.

definition: The process of legally creating a company through registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission, giving it a separate legal personality.
plainLanguageSummary: Registering your business with CAC so it becomes a legal company, separate from you as an individual. From then on, the company exists in its own right.

definition: An agreement or legal duty by one party to compensate another for specified losses, or to restore them to the position they were in before the loss occurred.
plainLanguageSummary: A promise to make good someone's loss. In contracts and insurance, the indemnifier pays the injured party's losses up to the agreed amount.

definition: Legal protection for the ornamental or aesthetic aspect of a manufactured article, granted through registration under the Patents and Designs Act.
plainLanguageSummary: Protecting how a product looks. Register your design (like a distinctive bottle shape) and others cannot copy its appearance without permission.
citations: Patents and Designs Act, Cap P2, LFN 2004

definition: A court order requiring a person to do or refrain from doing a specified act. It may be interim, interlocutory or perpetual, and may be prohibitory or mandatory.
plainLanguageSummary: A court order that tells someone to stop doing something (or to do something). For example, stopping a company from polluting your land while the case continues.

definition: The state of a person or company that cannot pay its debts as they fall due, or whose liabilities exceed assets. It triggers insolvency procedures such as liquidation or bankruptcy.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone or a business cannot pay its bills. The law provides orderly ways of dealing with the fall out, like winding up the company.

definition: An arrangement where a person pays a premium to an insurer who compensates them for specified losses or risks, under the terms of an insurance policy. Certain policies are mandatory in Nigeria.
plainLanguageSummary: Paying a small, regular amount so that a big loss is covered when disaster hits, like car or home insurance. Some types are legally required.
citations: Insurance Act 2003; National Insurance Commission guidelines

definition: Creations of the mind , inventions, literary and artistic works, designs, symbols, and names , that are protected by law through patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets.
plainLanguageSummary: The law protects things you create with your brain. Your songs, your inventions, your brand logo, your app code , someone can't just steal them. You get exclusive rights to use and profit from your creations.
citations: Copyright Act 2022; Trade Marks Act, Cap T13, LFN 2004; Patents and Designs Act, Cap P2, LFN 2004

definition: An application made during the course of a case, before final judgment, asking the court to take a procedural or interim step, such as granting an injunction or striking out a claim.
plainLanguageSummary: A side request you make while the main case is still running, like 'stop them from selling the property before judgment'. It deals with interim issues, not the final outcome.

definition: The state of dying without a valid will. When a person dies intestate, their estate is distributed according to statutory rules of succession rather than their personal wishes.
plainLanguageSummary: Dying without a will. When that happens, the government decides who gets your property based on fixed rules , usually spouse and children first. It's not always what you'd have wanted.
citations: Administration of Estates Laws (various states); Wills Act, Cap W2, LFN 2004

definition: The power of a court to accept certain facts as true without requiring proof, because they are so well known or verifiable that proof would be unnecessary.
plainLanguageSummary: Some facts a court accepts automatically without evidence, like that Nigeria is a federation or certain official gazettes. It saves time on things everyone knows.

definition: The power of courts to examine the actions of the legislative, executive, and administrative arms of government and determine whether they are consistent with the constitution.
plainLanguageSummary: Courts can check whether the government is playing by the rules. If a law or government action violates the Constitution, the courts can strike it down. It's the judiciary keeping everyone else in check.

definition: The authority given to a legal court to hear and determine a case. It defines the geographic area, subject matter, and persons over which a court can exercise its judicial power.
plainLanguageSummary: Every court has a 'territory' , a specific area or type of case it handles. A local court can't try a federal crime, and a Lagos court can't handle a case from Kano. Jurisdiction decides who hears what.

definition: The unlawful taking and detention of a person against their will, often to demand a ransom. It is a serious felony with severe penalties in Nigeria.
plainLanguageSummary: Forcibly taking and holding someone, usually demanding money for their release. It carries very heavy punishment because of how common and harmful it is.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Various state anti-kidnapping laws

definition: The federal statute vesting all land in each state in the Governor, who holds it in trust for the people. It governs how land is allocated, held, transferred and developed in Nigeria.
plainLanguageSummary: The law that owns all land: in every state, land technically belongs to the Governor who holds it in trust for the people. It is why you need documents like Certificates of Occupancy for land.
citations: Land Use Act, Cap L5, LFN 2004

definition: A contract granting a person (the lessee) the right to use and occupy another's land or property (the lessor's) for a specified period, in exchange for rent.
plainLanguageSummary: Renting rather than owning: a lease lets you use property for a set time while someone else keeps ownership. You pay rent and follow the agreement.

definition: A bank's undertaking to pay a seller a sum of money on behalf of a buyer when the seller presents the required documents, commonly used in international trade.
plainLanguageSummary: A bank promise that a seller will be paid after shipping goods if they present the right papers. It reduces risk in cross-border deals.
citations: Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600)

definition: A published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written or broadcast form of defamation.
plainLanguageSummary: Defamation that's in writing , a newspaper article, a social media post, a YouTube video. If someone publishes lies about you that hurt your reputation, that's libel and you can sue.

definition: State-level legislation that prescribes the time limits within which civil actions must be commenced. The specific periods vary by state and by type of claim.
plainLanguageSummary: Each state in Nigeria has its own rules about how long you have to file a lawsuit. These time limits vary , some give you 6 years, others 12. If you miss the deadline, your case is dead.
citations: Limitation Laws of various Nigerian states

definition: The protection that shareholders of a limited company enjoy: their personal liability for company debts is capped at the amount unpaid on their shares.
plainLanguageSummary: If the company fails, creditors can only take the company's assets, not the owners' personal property. Your risk is limited to what you invested.

definition: A fixed sum agreed in a contract as the genuine pre-estimate of loss for a specified breach, payable upon that breach. Courts enforce it if it is not a penalty.
plainLanguageSummary: A contract stating the exact amount to pay if someone breaks a specific part of the deal, like a builder paying per day of delay. It must be a fair estimate, not punishment.

definition: The formal winding up of a company's affairs: its assets are sold, debts are paid in order of priority, and the company is dissolved.
plainLanguageSummary: Closing a company permanently: selling what it owns, paying creditors in order and then removing the company from existence.
citations: Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, Part XV

definition: Latin for 'standing'. The right of a person to bring an action or appear in court. A court will not hear a matter from someone with no sufficient interest or connection to it.
plainLanguageSummary: You must have a real connection or interest in a case before you can sue. You cannot randomly take someone to court over a matter that does not affect you.
citations: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999

definition: The unlawful killing of a human being without malice aforethought. It may be voluntary (in circumstances of provocation) or involuntary (through criminal negligence or an unlawful act).
plainLanguageSummary: Causing someone's death without planning it: either through a sudden loss of control, or through careless, negligent conduct that kills.

definition: An interim court order freezing a defendant's assets (including bank accounts) to stop them from disposing of assets before judgment or enforcement.
plainLanguageSummary: A 'freeze order'. Before judgment, you can ask the court to freeze someone's money and property so they cannot hide it before you win your case.
citations: Common law; Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria Act 2010

definition: A legally recognised union of two persons, either under the Marriage Act, customary law or Islamic law. Its validity depends on the form of marriage contracted.
plainLanguageSummary: Legal union between two people. In Nigeria it can be under the Act (registry), under native custom, or under Islamic law, each with its own rules.

definition: A voluntary process where a neutral third party (the mediator) helps disputing parties negotiate a mutually acceptable resolution. Unlike arbitration, the mediator does not impose a decision.
plainLanguageSummary: A trained neutral person helps you and the other side talk it out and find a solution you both agree on. The mediator doesn't decide who's right , they just help you find common ground.

definition: The founding document of a company stating its name, address, objectives and share capital, setting the boundaries within which the company may act.
plainLanguageSummary: The company's birth certificate. It says what the company is called, what it does and how much capital it can raise. Acts outside it can be ultra vires.

definition: Latin for 'guilty mind'. The mental element of a crime, such as intent, knowledge or recklessness, that must generally accompany the guilty act for a conviction.
plainLanguageSummary: The 'guilty mind'. For most crimes, the person must have meant to do wrong or known it was wrong. Accidents without any guilty intent are usually not crimes.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act

definition: The lowest remuneration that employers are legally required to pay workers, set by law (nationally and by state) with special exceptions for small businesses and part-time work.
plainLanguageSummary: The least someone can legally be paid for their work. Paying below it is a violation. It is reviewed and set by law.

definition: A crime less serious than a felony, usually punishable by a shorter prison term, a fine, or community service rather than long imprisonment.
plainLanguageSummary: A smaller crime, like petty theft or disorderly conduct. The punishment is lighter, often a fine or brief jail time.

definition: A false statement of fact made by one party that induces another to enter a contract. It may be fraudulent, negligent or innocent, and can make the contract voidable.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone sells a deal on a lie that convinced you to sign. If the statement was false and important, you may cancel the contract or claim damages.

definition: The process of making illegally obtained funds appear legitimate through placement, layering and integration. It is a serious offence in Nigeria punishable by heavy penalties.
plainLanguageSummary: Cleaning dirty money: taking proceeds of crime and passing them through legitimate-looking channels so the source is hidden. It is a serious federal crime.

definition: A security interest taken over property by a lender to secure a loan, giving the lender the right to sell the property if the borrower defaults on repayment.
plainLanguageSummary: Using your house as security for a loan. You keep the house while paying, but if you stop paying, the bank can sell it to recover its money.
citations: Mortgage Institutions Act; Property and Commercial Laws

definition: The unlawful killing of a human being with malice aforethought, that is, with the intention to kill or cause grievous bodily harm. It is the most serious crime under Nigerian law.
plainLanguageSummary: Killing someone on purpose or meaning to hurt them badly enough that they die. The most serious case in criminal law, punishable by the severest penalties.
citations: Criminal Code Act, Section 316; Penal Code Act

definition: The federal legislature of Nigeria, consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives. Its primary functions are lawmaking, oversight of the executive and control of public funds.
plainLanguageSummary: The two-chamber lawmaking body at the federal level: the Senate and the House of Representatives. They make federal laws, approve budgets and hold the executive to account.

definition: Failure to exercise the standard of care that a reasonably prudent person would have exercised in a similar situation. It is the basis of most personal injury claims.
plainLanguageSummary: Being careless when you should have been careful. If a doctor makes a mistake that any good doctor wouldn't make, or a driver runs a red light , that's negligence, and the person who got hurt can claim damages.
citations: Common law; Donoghue v Stevenson [1932] AC 562

definition: A voluntary, informal dispute resolution method where the parties, with or without counsel, seek to reach agreement directly without involving a third party.
plainLanguageSummary: The parties talk directly and try to agree, with or without lawyers. No third party decides: both sides must accept the outcome.

definition: The formal abandonment of a criminal prosecution by the Attorney General, ending the proceedings. It is distinct from an acquittal because the charge may be brought again.
plainLanguageSummary: When the Attorney General formally drops a criminal case before a verdict. The defendant walks free, though the state could technically press charges again.

definition: The replacement of one party to a contract with a new party, by the agreement of all parties, transferring the rights and obligations to the newcomer.
plainLanguageSummary: Trading one party for another in a deal with everyone's consent. After novation, the old party is out and the new one takes over the obligations.

definition: An unreasonable interference with another person's use or enjoyment of their land or property, such as excessive noise, fumes or obstruction. It may be public or private.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone's activity unreasonably disturb you, like constant noise or fumes from the workshop next door. You can sue to stop it or recover damages.
citations: Common law principles; various environmental statutes

definition: A solemn declaration or promise, invoking a deity or something sacred, to fulfil a duty or speak the truth. In legal proceedings, oaths are required for affidavits and witness testimony.
plainLanguageSummary: When you raise your hand and swear to tell the truth, or sign a document saying you've told the truth , that's an oath. Breaking an oath is a crime called perjury.
citations: Evidence Act 2011; Oaths Act, Cap O1, LFN 2004

definition: Latin for 'said by the way'. A remark or opinion in a judgment that is not essential to the decision. It is persuasive but not binding on later courts.
plainLanguageSummary: When a judge adds side comments or opinions in a ruling that are not needed for the decision itself. These comments can influence later cases but do not bind other courts.

definition: An act or omission prohibited by law and punishable by the state, such as by fine, imprisonment or both. Offences may be strict liability or require a guilty mind.
plainLanguageSummary: Anything the law says you must not do and punishes you for doing. It can be minor like a traffic ticket or serious like armed robbery.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act

definition: The two essential elements of a contract: an offer is a definite proposal made by one party, and acceptance is the unconditional agreement to that proposal.
plainLanguageSummary: One person says 'I'll do this for you at this price' (offer), and the other says 'deal' (acceptance). Once both sides agree on the same terms, a contract is formed.

definition: The power of a court to hear a case for the first time, as opposed to appellate jurisdiction where a higher court reviews a decision from a lower court.
plainLanguageSummary: Some courts get to hear a case right from the start , that's their first shot at it. The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in disputes between states or between the federal government and a state.

definition: A way to start civil proceedings for questions of law or construction that do not require substantial disputes of fact, decided mainly through affidavits rather than full trial.
plainLanguageSummary: A faster way to start a court case when the argument is about a legal question, not facts. Both sides file sworn statements, and the judge decides on points of law without a long trial.

definition: The conditional release of a convicted prisoner before the end of their sentence, subject to supervision and conditions. Breach of conditions can lead to return to custody.
plainLanguageSummary: Releasing a prisoner early on condition they follow rules and check in with authorities. Breaking the conditions sends them back to prison.

definition: A business relationship where two or more persons run a business together, sharing profits and losses. Unless limited, partners are jointly liable for the firm's debts.
plainLanguageSummary: Two or more people running a business together and sharing the gains. In an ordinary partnership, each partner is personally responsible for the firm's debts.

definition: A common law wrong where one trader misrepresents their goods or services as those of another, damaging goodwill. It protects unregistered brands against imitations.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone builds their business on your reputation by pretending to be you. You can sue them even without a registered trademark if customers are being fooled.

definition: A exclusive right granted for an invention, providing the patent holder with the right to decide how the invention can be used by others for a limited period.
plainLanguageSummary: If you invent something new and useful, you can get a patent that gives you exclusive rights to it for 20 years. Others can't make, sell, or use your invention without your permission.
citations: Patents and Designs Act, Cap P2, LFN 2004

definition: The statute defining criminal offences and punishments applicable in the northern states of Nigeria, alongside the Criminal Code which applies in the south.
plainLanguageSummary: The companion crime law used in the northern states. It defines what counts as a crime and what punishment fits, covering similar offences to the Criminal Code.
citations: Penal Code (Northern States) Federal Provisions Act, Cap P3, LFN 2004

definition: The offence of deliberately making a false statement under oath or affirmation in legal proceedings.
plainLanguageSummary: Lying in court or in a sworn document. If you promise to tell the truth and then don't, that's perjury , a serious criminal offence that can land you in prison.
citations: Criminal Code Act, Section 117; Penal Code Act, Section 191

definition: The right of a foreign national to live and work in a country indefinitely without being a citizen, entitling them to most rights except voting and full political office.
plainLanguageSummary: A non-citizen's right to live permanently in a country. You can stay and work, but you still cannot vote or hold some political posts.

definition: A tax charged on the income of individuals and some partnerships, including salaries, business profits and investment income, governed by the Personal Income Tax Act.
plainLanguageSummary: Tax on what an individual earns, whether salary or business income. Your employer may deduct it at source (PAYE), or you file it yourself.
citations: Personal Income Tax Act, Cap P8, LFN 2004

definition: An agreement between the prosecutor and defendant whereby the defendant pleads guilty to a lesser charge or receives a lighter sentence in exchange for cooperation.
plainLanguageSummary: A deal in criminal cases: instead of going to trial and risking a heavy sentence, the accused agrees to plead guilty to a lesser offence. The prosecution saves time, and the accused gets a lighter punishment.
citations: Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015, Sections 270-275

definition: The introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment (air, water or land) in quantities that damage health or ecosystems. It is regulated and punishable under environmental law.
plainLanguageSummary: Dirtying the air, water or land so it harms people or nature. Polluters can face sanctions, clean-up orders and suits from affected communities.
citations: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) Act 2007

definition: A legal document authorizing one person (the agent or attorney-in-fact) to act on behalf of another (the principal) in legal or financial matters.
plainLanguageSummary: You write a letter saying 'this person can make decisions for me.' If you're travelling or unable to handle your own affairs, you can give someone you trust the legal authority to act on your behalf.
citations: Land Use Act 1978; Powers of Attorney Act, Cap P5, LFN 2004

definition: A previous judicial decision used as authority to decide later similar cases. Binding precedents must be followed; persuasive ones may be considered but need not be followed.
plainLanguageSummary: Earlier court decisions guide later ones. If a similar case was already decided a certain way, a judge will usually decide yours the same way for consistency.

definition: The principle that every person accused of an offence is presumed innocent until proven guilty by a court of law. The prosecution must establish guilt, not the accused innocence.
plainLanguageSummary: You are innocent until a court says otherwise. It is the government's job to prove you guilty, not your job to prove you are innocent.

definition: A legal right to withhold certain communications from disclosure in court, such as lawyer-client communications, marital communications and state secrets.
plainLanguageSummary: Some conversations the law protects so they cannot be dragged into court, the most famous being the confidentiality between a lawyer and their client.

definition: The principle that only parties to a contract may enforce or be bound by its terms. Third parties generally cannot sue or be sued on a contract they are not part of.
plainLanguageSummary: Only the people who signed a deal can enforce it or be bound by it. A third person cannot jump in to sue on a contract they never made.

definition: The legal process of proving a will is valid and distributing the deceased person's estate according to the will or, in the absence of a will, according to intestacy laws.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone dies, someone has to go to court to prove the will is real and then make sure their property goes to the right people. That whole court process is called probate.
citations: Wills Act, Cap W2, LFN 2004; Administration of Estates Laws (various states)

definition: A court order allowing an offender to remain in the community instead of prison, under supervision and subject to conditions, such as reporting to an officer or completing treatment.
plainLanguageSummary: Instead of jail, a court lets you stay free but under watch. You must follow conditions and report regularly, and misbehaving lands you in prison.
citations: Criminal Code Act; various states statutes

definition: The legal liability of manufacturers, distributors and sellers for injuries caused by defective or unsafe products, whether through negligence, breach of warranty or strict liability.
plainLanguageSummary: If a product you bought is dangerous or defective and hurts you, the maker or seller can be held responsible and you can claim compensation.
citations: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018

definition: The formal ending of a session of the legislature by the President or Governor without dissolving it. Pending business temporarily lapses and is resumed in the next session.
plainLanguageSummary: A formal pause in parliament's session called by the President or a Governor. Meetings stop for a period, and unfinished business can restart in the next session.

definition: The institution and conduct of criminal proceedings against an accused person on behalf of the state, usually by the Attorney General or the police.
plainLanguageSummary: When the government takes someone to court for a crime. The state brings the case, and the accused defends against it.

definition: Legal action brought to protect the rights and interests of the public or a group, rather than the personal interests of the claimant, often involving rights, environment or governance matters.
plainLanguageSummary: Suing to protect the public good or a group of people, not just yourself. Courts now allow broader standing in such cases, like fighting pollution or rights abuse.

definition: The legal reasoning or rule of law on which a judicial decision is based. It is the binding part of a judgment that later courts must follow.
plainLanguageSummary: The core reason a judge decided a case the way they did. This reason is the part that becomes the rule other courts must follow, not the judge's side comments.

definition: The questioning of a witness again by the party that called them, after cross-examination, to clarify or explain matters that arose during cross-examination.
plainLanguageSummary: After the other side finishes probing your witness, your own lawyer can ask follow-up questions to clear up any confusion or damage caused.

definition: The withdrawal of a judge from hearing a case because of bias, conflict of interest or a reasonable appearance of bias. The judge may step down voluntarily or upon application.
plainLanguageSummary: When a judge steps aside from a case because they might not be impartial, like if they know one of the parties. It protects everyone's right to a fair hearing.

definition: The detention of a suspect in custody pending further investigation or trial, when bail has been refused or is not available for the type of offence charged.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone is kept in custody because they can't get bail , maybe the crime is too serious or the court thinks they might flee. They stay in prison waiting for the next court date.

definition: The fundamental right of every person to a fair and public hearing within a reasonable time by an independent and impartial court or tribunal established by law.
plainLanguageSummary: If you are taken to court, you get a fair chance: a neutral judge, a public hearing, time to prepare, and the right to state your side. Courts cannot rush or hide your case.

definition: The fundamental right of every person not to be deprived of life intentionally, save in execution of a sentence of death imposed by a court. It is protected under the Constitution.
plainLanguageSummary: The most basic right: nobody can take your life intentionally. The state cannot kill you except as a lawful court-ordered punishment. Your life is protected by the Constitution.

definition: The fundamental right of every person to respect for their private and family life, home and correspondence. It protects personal information and communications from unlawful intrusion.
plainLanguageSummary: Your home, phone messages and private life are protected. The state cannot spy on you, search you or share your private information without lawful justification.

definition: An unlawful assembly that has begun to disturb the peace or includes the use or threat of violence. Participants may be prosecuted for riotous behaviour.
plainLanguageSummary: A mob that stops being peaceful and turns violent or destructive. Being part of a riot is a serious offence, even if you were not the ringleader.

definition: The principle that all people and institutions are subject to and accountable to law that is fairly applied and enforced. No one is above the law, including government officials.
plainLanguageSummary: Nobody is bigger than the law , not the president, not a judge, not anyone. The law applies equally to everyone, and everyone has to play by the same rules.

definition: The rescue of a ship, its cargo or passengers from danger at sea, with the rescuer entitled to a salvage reward based on the value saved and the risk involved.
plainLanguageSummary: Saving a ship or its cargo from danger at sea. The rescuer earns a reward calculated from the value of what was saved.

definition: The government's power to search a person's property and seize evidence of a crime, generally requiring a warrant supported by probable cause.
plainLanguageSummary: The police can search your house and take things , but only if they have a good reason and usually a warrant from a judge. If they search without a warrant, whatever they find might not be usable in court.

definition: A legal justification for using reasonable force to protect oneself or others from an imminent attack. The force used must be proportionate to the threat.
plainLanguageSummary: You may use reasonable force to defend yourself or someone else from danger. The force must be no more than needed to stop the attack.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act

definition: The punishment given to a person convicted of a crime by a court. Sentences can include imprisonment, fines, community service, probation, or a combination thereof.
plainLanguageSummary: What happens after you're found guilty. The judge decides your punishment , it could be time in prison, a fine, community service, or a mix. The seriousness of the crime and your history matter.
citations: Criminal Code Act; Penal Code Act; ACJA 2015

definition: The division of government responsibilities into distinct branches , executive, legislative, and judicial , to prevent any one branch from exercising the core functions of another.
plainLanguageSummary: The government is split into three parts: the ones who make laws (National Assembly), the ones who enforce them (Executive/President), and the ones who judge disputes (Courts). Each stays in its lane.

definition: The formal delivery of court documents (such as a summons or claim) to a party so they have official notice of proceedings against them. Proper service is required before a court can act.
plainLanguageSummary: Court papers must be officially delivered to the person being sued or charged. If they were not properly served, they might not even know about the case, and the court cannot just proceed unfairly.
citations: Sheriffs and Civil Process Act, Cap S6, LFN 2004

definition: Non-consensual sexual contact or behaviour inflicted on a person, including rape. Nigerian law criminalises rape, sexual coercion and related offences regardless of gender.
plainLanguageSummary: Any unwanted sexual act forced on someone, including rape. Consent matters: if it was not freely given, it is an offence. Both men and women are protected.
citations: Criminal Code Act, Section 357; Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act 2015

definition: A person who owns shares in a company, giving them rights to dividends, voting and a share of assets on liquidation, in proportion to their shareholding.
plainLanguageSummary: A part-owner of a company. Shareholders get dividends, vote at meetings and share the leftovers if the company folds.

definition: An appellate court established in some states that hears civil appeals involving Islamic personal law, such as marriage, inheritance and family relations between Muslims.
plainLanguageSummary: Where states have it, this court handles appeals on Islamic personal law cases like inheritance and marriage between Muslims. It operates alongside the regular courts.

definition: A false spoken statement that damages a person's reputation; the oral form of defamation.
plainLanguageSummary: Defamation that's spoken , someone tells lies about you face-to-face or in a speech. It's harder to prove than libel because there's no written record, but you can still sue.

definition: A court designed to handle low-value civil disputes quickly, cheaply and without lawyers, using simplified procedures. Nigeria is progressively introducing these courts for consumer and small debt cases.
plainLanguageSummary: A fast, simple court for small money disputes like unpaid debts or faulty purchases. The process is short, cheap and usually no lawyer is needed.
citations: Lagos Small Claims Court Practice Directions 2021; other state rules

definition: A business owned and run by one person who is personally liable for all its debts and obligations, usually registered simply as a business name.
plainLanguageSummary: A one-person business. All profits are yours, but so are all debts: if the business owes money, you personally owe it.

definition: A principle that a state cannot generally be sued in the courts of another state without its consent, subject to exceptions for commercial activities and certain waivers.
plainLanguageSummary: You usually cannot drag a foreign government into your local courts. Exceptions exist, especially when states engage in commercial business.
citations: State Immunity Act 2009 (United Kingdom pattern); customary international law

definition: A court order compelling a party to perform their contractual obligation exactly as promised, instead of paying damages. It is discretionary and used where damages are inadequate, especially for land.
plainLanguageSummary: A court forcing someone to do exactly what they promised, rather than just paying compensation. Courts order it, chiefly for unique things like land.

definition: Periodic payments ordered by a court for the maintenance of a spouse after divorce or separation, based on the needs of the recipient and the capacity of the payer.
plainLanguageSummary: Money one ex-spouse pays the other to keep supporting them after a divorce. It depends on need on one side and ability to pay on the other.
citations: Matrimonial Causes Act, Cap M7, LFN 2004

definition: The degree of certainty required to prove a fact in court. Criminal cases require proof beyond reasonable doubt; civil cases require proof on a balance of probabilities.
plainLanguageSummary: How sure the court must be. In a criminal case, very sure (beyond reasonable doubt). In a civil case, just 'more likely than not'.

definition: The doctrine that courts should follow the principles established in earlier similar cases (precedents). Lower courts are bound by the decisions of higher courts.
plainLanguageSummary: Courts stick to earlier decisions on the same point. If the Supreme Court decided a question, every other court follows it. This makes the law predictable and fair.

definition: The highest court of first instance in a state, with jurisdiction over civil and criminal matters arising under state law, including land disputes and most criminal trials.
plainLanguageSummary: The main trial court in each state. Land disputes, serious criminal cases and most civil suing start here. Each state has its own High Court.

definition: The document filed by a plaintiff that sets out the facts, details and reliefs (remedies) they are seeking from the court.
plainLanguageSummary: When you sue someone, this is your side of the story on paper: what happened, why it is the other side's fault, and exactly what you want the court to do.
