definition: A law that sets the maximum time after an event within which legal proceedings may be initiated. Once the time limit expires, the claim is usually barred.
plainLanguageSummary: There's a deadline for filing lawsuits. If you wait too long, you lose the right to sue. For example, you usually have 6 years to sue over a contract breach, but only 3 months for an election petition.
citations: Limitation Law, Cap L9, LFN 2004 (varies by state)

definition: A court order suspending the enforcement of a judgment pending an appeal or further order, preventing the winning party from enforcing the judgment in the meantime.
plainLanguageSummary: If you lose a case but are appealing, you can ask the court to pause enforcement, so the winner cannot seize your property or collect money until the appeal is decided.

definition: An offence where guilt does not require proof of mens rea: committing the prohibited act is enough. It is common in regulatory offences such as traffic and food safety laws.
plainLanguageSummary: Some minor 'regulatory' crimes do not need you to have meant it. Driving over the limit or selling expired food is an offence regardless of intent.
citations: Criminal Code Act; various regulatory statutes

definition: A court order compelling a person to attend court to give evidence or to bring specified documents. Failure to comply can amount to contempt of court.
plainLanguageSummary: A court order saying you must appear and testify, or bring certain papers. If you ignore it, you can be punished for contempt of court.

definition: The right of an insurer who has paid a claim to step into the insured's shoes and pursue the person responsible for the loss to recover what was paid out.
plainLanguageSummary: After your insurer pays you for a loss caused by someone else, they can chase that person for the money. Your right to claim passes to the insurer.

definition: The order and rules by which a deceased person's property passes to others, whether by will (testate succession) or by law when there is no will (intestate succession).
plainLanguageSummary: Who gets your property when you die. If you leave a will, it follows your wishes; if not, the law decides using fixed succession rules.
citations: Administration of Estates Laws (various states); Wills Act

definition: A judgment entered without a full trial when the court is satisfied that the defendant has no real prospect of defending the claim and there is no need for a trial.
plainLanguageSummary: When a case is so clear-cut that a full trial would be a waste of time, the court can decide immediately. Used when the other side obviously has no real defence.

definition: A court document requiring a person to appear in court at a specified time, either as a defendant to answer a claim or as a party in proceedings.
plainLanguageSummary: The court sends you a paper telling you to come to court and answer a case. Ignoring a summons can lead to a judgment against you without your side heard.

definition: The highest court in Nigeria and the final court of appeal. It has final appellate jurisdiction and original jurisdiction in disputes between the Federation and states or between states.
plainLanguageSummary: The top court in the country. Its decisions are final and bind every other court. When all appeals are exhausted, the Supreme Court is where the case ends.

definition: A person believed to have committed a crime but who has not yet been charged or convicted. A suspect retains all fundamental rights until proven guilty by a court of law.
plainLanguageSummary: Someone the police think did something wrong. But thinking isn't proving , a suspect is innocent until the court says otherwise. They still have rights, including the right to a lawyer.

definition: A written statement made under oath or affirmation, similar to an affidavit but sometimes used in less formal legal contexts or administrative proceedings.
plainLanguageSummary: Like an affidavit but sometimes used in simpler situations , like when you're making a statement to a government agency. You still swear it's true, and lying is still perjury.

definition: Arranging one's affairs lawfully to reduce tax liability, such as using permitted reliefs and deductions. It is legal, unlike tax evasion, but is scrutinised by tax authorities.
plainLanguageSummary: Reducing your tax bill using legal options like allowable deductions. It is lawful, though courts may strike down artificial schemes designed only to avoid tax.
citations: Companies Income Tax Act; Personal Income Tax Act

definition: The deliberate, illegal non-payment or underpayment of tax, such as hiding income or falsifying records. It is a criminal offence punishable by fines and imprisonment.
plainLanguageSummary: Cheating on your taxes on purpose, like not declaring income or faking records. It is a crime that can end in fines or jail.
citations: Companies Income Tax Act; Personal Income Tax Act

definition: The system by which government levies and collects compulsory payments from persons and businesses to fund public services, administered through federal and state tax authorities.
plainLanguageSummary: The way government takes its share to pay for roads, schools and services. Income, goods and company profits are common bases for taxation.

definition: The right to occupy and use a property created by a lease or agreement, subject to payment of rent and observance of the landlord and tenant relationship.
plainLanguageSummary: The arrangement where a tenant occupies a landlord's property. Rent, notice periods and repair duties are all governed by tenancy rules.
citations: Recovery of Premises Laws (various states); Tenancy Laws

definition: The dishonest taking of property belonging to another, with the intention of permanently depriving the owner of it. It is known also as stealing.
plainLanguageSummary: Taking someone's property dishonestly and intending to keep it. Picking a pocket, snatching a phone or emptying a shop till are all theft.
citations: Criminal Code Act, Sections 383-386; Penal Code Act

definition: The legal right to own, occupy and dispose of land or property, evidenced by documents such as a Certificate of Occupancy, deed or instrument of title.
plainLanguageSummary: Proof of ownership of land or property. Who holds good title holds the right to the land, and messy title is the biggest source of land disputes.
citations: Land Use Act, Cap L5, LFN 2004

definition: A civil wrong that causes someone else to suffer loss or harm, resulting in legal liability for the person who commits the tortious act. Examples include negligence, defamation, and nuisance.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone does something wrong (but it's not a crime) and it hurts you. Like if a shop leaves a wet floor and you slip, or someone spreads lies about you. You can sue them for damages.
citations: Common law principles; various Nigerian statutes

definition: Confidential business information that gives a competitive advantage, such as formulas, methods and customer lists. Protection depends on keeping it secret.
plainLanguageSummary: Valuable business secrets like recipes or client lists. No registration needed; protection comes from keeping them confidential and suing if they leak.

definition: An organisation of workers formed to protect and advance their interests regarding wages, working conditions and other employment matters, and recognised under labour law.
plainLanguageSummary: Workers banding together to negotiate better pay and conditions. Unions have legal rights to represent members and bargain with employers.
citations: Trade Unions Act, Cap T14, LFN 2004

definition: A recognizable sign, design, or expression that identifies products or services of a particular source and distinguishes them from others.
plainLanguageSummary: That logo, name, or symbol that makes your brand yours. When you register it, no one else can use something similar to confuse customers. Think of the Nike swoosh or the Coca-Cola script.
citations: Trade Marks Act, Cap T13, LFN 2004

definition: A formal, binding agreement between sovereign states, or between states and international organisations, governing matters such as trade, human rights or extradition.
plainLanguageSummary: A deal between countries that binds them legally. Nigeria participates in many, from human rights agreements to trade pacts.
citations: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969

definition: An unlawful intrusion on another person's land, body or goods. Trespass to land, person (assault and battery) and chattels are actionable without proof of actual damage.
plainLanguageSummary: Entering someone's property without permission, or interfering with their person or belongings. Even without real harm, trespass is actionable.

definition: A legal arrangement where one party (the trustee) holds property or assets for the benefit of another (the beneficiary), subject to specific terms and obligations.
plainLanguageSummary: Someone gives you something valuable to hold and manage for someone else's benefit. You don't own it , you're just the custodian. If you misuse it, the law will hold you accountable.

definition: A Latin term meaning 'beyond the powers'. It describes an act done without legal authority, such as a government body or company acting outside the powers granted to it. Such acts are void.
plainLanguageSummary: Means 'beyond the powers'. When a company or the government does something it was never legally allowed to do, the action has no legal effect. Doing the right thing the wrong way counts too.

definition: Unfair pressure or manipulation in a relationship of trust (such as between solicitor and client, doctor and patient) that leaves a contract voidable.
plainLanguageSummary: When someone in a position of trust pressure you into an unfair deal, like a caregiver using their hold over an elderly relative.

definition: The termination of an employee without just cause or due process, in violation of the terms of employment, statute or collective agreement. Remedies include reinstatement or compensation.
plainLanguageSummary: Getting fired without a real reason or without following the right process. If you are treated this way, you can claim reinstatement or compensation.

definition: Deceptive, misleading or fraudulent business conduct, such as false advertising, bait-and-switch, counterfeiting and unconscionable sales tactics. They are prohibited by consumer protection law.
plainLanguageSummary: Business tricks that cheat customers: fake ads, bait-and-switch, counterfeit goods. Consumer law lets you report these and claim remedies.
citations: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018

definition: A gathering of three or more persons in a manner that disturbs the peace or gives reasonable grounds to fear a breach of the peace, and that does not disperse when lawfully required.
plainLanguageSummary: Three or more people gathering in a way that threatens public disturbance and refusing to disperse when told. A peaceful, lawful protest is different.

definition: A consumption tax charged on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production and distribution, ultimately borne by the final consumer.
plainLanguageSummary: A tax added at each stage of a product's journey, which ends up in the price you pay in a shop. Businesses collect it for the government.
citations: Value Added Tax Act, Cap V1, LFN 2004

definition: The constitutional power of the President to refuse to sign a Bill passed by the National Assembly, preventing it from becoming law unless the Assembly overrides the veto by a two-thirds majority.
plainLanguageSummary: When the President refuses to sign a law that parliament passed. Parliament can still force it through, but only with a big majority. It is part of the checks and balances system.

definition: Liability imposed on one person (usually an employer) for wrongs committed by another (usually an employee) in the course of their employment.
plainLanguageSummary: An employer can be held responsible for the wrongs their staff commit while doing their jobs. The company, not just the worker, faces liability.

definition: The rights of crime victims to be informed, heard and protected during criminal proceedings, and to seek restitution or compensation for harm suffered.
plainLanguageSummary: If you are the victim of a crime, you have a say. You can be heard in court, be protected from the accused, and ask for compensation for injury or loss.
citations: Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015, Sections 298-305

definition: The crime of causing physical, sexual, psychological or economic harm to another person, as defined under the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act. It covers domestic violence, harmful widowhood practices and forced removal of organs.
plainLanguageSummary: Hurting another person physically, sexually, mentally or financially. The law prohibits things like beating a partner, harmful rituals and similar forms of abuse.

definition: A contract that has no legal effect from the start because it is legally impossible or prohibited, such as a contract to commit a crime or one made by a person lacking capacity.
plainLanguageSummary: An agreement the law treats as if it never existed, like a deal to commit a crime. Neither party can enforce it.

definition: A contract that is valid but may be set aside by one party because it was entered under duress, undue influence, misrepresentation or mistake.
plainLanguageSummary: A real contract, but one side can cancel it if they were pressured, misled or taken advantage of when agreeing.

definition: A written order issued by a judge or magistrate that authorises law enforcement to make an arrest, search a premises, or carry out another specific legal action.
plainLanguageSummary: A judge's written permission for the police to do something , like arrest someone or search your house. Without a warrant (in most cases), the police can't just barge in.
citations: Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015; Criminal Code Act

definition: A legal document in which a person (the testator) expresses their wishes regarding the distribution of their property and the care of any minor children after their death.
plainLanguageSummary: A written document that says what happens to your stuff when you die. Without one, the law decides for you , and it might not be what you wanted. Everyone should have a will.

definition: Tax deducted at source from payments such as interest, rent and professional fees, serving as an advance payment of the recipient's tax liability.
plainLanguageSummary: Tax taken before you receive certain payments, like rent or consultancy fees. It counts as an advance on your income tax bill.
citations: Companies Income Tax Act; Personal Income Tax Act

definition: A person who gives evidence in court, usually under oath. Witnesses may testify about what they saw, heard or did, or provide expert opinion in specialist matters.
plainLanguageSummary: Someone who gives evidence in court about what they know. You can be an eyewitness or an expert witness giving specialised opinion.

definition: The right of an employee to compensation for injury, disability or death arising from an accident at work or an occupational disease, per the Employees' Compensation Act.
plainLanguageSummary: If you are hurt on the job or fall ill because of work, the law says you must be compensated, even if you were partly at fault.

definition: A formal written order issued by a court commanding a person to do or refrain from doing something, or authorising a legal official to carry out a specified act.
plainLanguageSummary: A court document that orders someone to do something or stop doing something. Writs are the classic way courts make their authority felt, from arrests to halting actions.
